Recorded inverted endpoints and near-identical-condition disagreements motivate limited repeats rather than treating every extreme observation as a mechanistic finding.","batch_rationale":"The batch concentrates on relationships that remain distinguishable with the supplied catalog. The m125 volume pair and loading interpolation, m117 loading pair, m45 loading/ratio contrasts, m92 loading-solvent pair, and m80 and m94 loading extensions create comparisons that can teach interactions rather than merely add more retained compounds. The m134 pair directly tests a suspicious V1 regime. Intermediate-ratio aromatic ethers test a shared predicted V2 hump, with m116 providing a chemically relevant comparison whose predicted response differs. Alcohol, ether-acrylate, amino-acceptor, and benzophenone extensions connect these local experiments to other populated Row families. Two repeat-condition selections address specific evidence problems: the unusual m73 low-loading record and the m72 low-loading condition that the current model predicts substantially later than its measured anchor. Their adjacent-condition references help distinguish repeatability from genuine response changes. Existing neutral and heavy-atom labels already provide extensive ordinary-retention coverage, so additional such measurements are chosen only where they test a new response relationship, particularly ethers and donor-free carbonyls. This should improve overall V1/V2 learning by repairing conditional failures, learning endpoint-specific behavior, and reducing the chance that anomalous records induce broad corrections. Expected learning value remains a hypothesis: single-predictor quantiles are imperfect, repeated labels may retain unexplained variation, and absent experimental variables limit causal attribution."}
